cautions: RTG-O is never called AI or machine learning in the Port Houston release. Kaleris calls it RTG Optimization, part of its Advanced Optimization solution, aligned to RTG-O logic. Say optimization software that sequences and dispatches crane moves.
The phrase continuous learning in the release is about the teams learning during a slow rollout. It is not machine learning.
Kaleris's AI layer (Monitor and Prediction, Analysis Agent) belongs to Yard Intelligence Suite, launched May 12th, 2026. No source says Port Houston uses it.
Up to 20 percent is a ceiling and is reported by the vendor. Never say a flat 20 percent or call it independently measured.
The crane count depends on the date. The release says 142 RTGs, 2024 said 147, and the fleet reaches 163 with the March 2026 deliveries. Tie each number to its source and date.
The release says multi-phase deployment. The completion claim comes from Port Houston's 2025 year-end release (c27), which says full implementation happened in 2025, with no month given.
Kaleris dated the release January 6th, 2026 but its dateline typo reads January 6, 2025. Hellenic Shipping News reposted it January 8th, 2026. Use January 2026.
No wait-time or truck turn figure is credited to RTG-O. The roughly 40 minute average truck turn and 2.5 million trucks are port-wide 2025 numbers and must not be called results of the software.

Operators still run the cranes. Port Houston's RTGs are manned, ILA labor is named and the release mentions workflows for operators and dispatchers. Never call it automation or say it replaced workers. No source says exactly what each crane operator still does.
The No. 5 U.S. container port rank is for 2022 TEUs (announced May 2023). Give it as a 2022 ranking, never as current.
porthouston.com returned 403 to direct HTML fetches. c34 and c39 were read through a fetch tool that quotes fragments, so those quotes are partial excerpts and nothing longer.
The 2025 year-end release says $2.1 million in planned landside capital investment over five years, which looks like a typo for billion. Don't use it.
Neither terminal's county appears on any page fetched. Harris County is unverified here.

Sources disagree on punctuation. Hellenic Shipping News drops two serial commas the Kaleris original has, in 'more efficient RTG moves, and' and 'productivity, agility, and resilience'. Quote from the kaleris.com URL. The pages use curly apostrophes and quotation marks.
